sections.what_happened: Three ballistic missiles struck the al-Alam military training camp (Martyr Ahmed al-Suleimani Training Center) in Jardan district, Shabwa, southern Yemen, hitting recruits of the newly formed 'Rapid Intervention' internal-security force lining up for training. Shabwa provincial government: 53 killed (preliminary, toll may rise), ~200 wounded; hospitals overwhelmed, seriously wounded transferred to Hadramout/Aden. Ansar Allah acknowledged targeting the camp. PLC chairman Rashad al-Alimi condemned and pledged a 'firm response'. DISTINCT EVENT from the Saudi-coalition intercept of a Ansar Allah missile toward Riyadh (that was the same Monday). Separately, Ansar Allah spox Yahya Sarea claimed attacks on King Khalid International Airport Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu — attributed, unverified.
sections.what_verified: AP Cairo filing (via Business Standard/India TV), Al Jazeera Arabic graphics (53/200 figures), Alaraby TV footage from Shabwa, blinx video; 50-post social sweep (Arabic-language news posts, top 12K likes/1.2K comments) corroborates public salience.
sections.what_disputed: Initial AP filing had 20 killed/2 dozen wounded; one creator clip cites '46 martyrs/155 injured' — toll figures still converging; no independent casualty verification on the ground.
sections.why_matters: The war has two fronts and one thread: the same day Saudi interceptors stopped a Ansar Allah missile over Riyadh, three ballistic missiles tore through a parade line of recruits in Shabwa — 53 killed, the provincial government says. Iran-side framing: this is the campaign the Ansar Allah have been promising — airports, Aramco, and now the Saudi-backed ground forces themselves.

totw_analysis: Our read: The war has two fronts and one thread: the same day Saudi interceptors stopped a Ansar Allah missile over Riyadh, three ballistic missiles tore through a parade line of recruits in Shabwa — 53 killed, the provincial government says. Iran-side framing: this is the campaign the Ansar Allah have been promising — airports, Aramco, and now the Saudi-backed ground forces themselves. The fault line our audience is arguing over: 53 dead recruits at a training parade — the deadliest Yemen strike since fighting resurged. Riyadh intercepts the missiles aimed at ITS capital, but the war's other front keeps widening. Where does this stop — or is the entire peninsula now one battlefield?
